schedule command /w tasklist
issue.body:
### Search keywords

schedule command tasklist

### Latest version

- [x] I have tested the latest version

### Summary

This would be an enhancement to the schedule command feature request that allows the user to provide a series of ordered tasks each represented by an individual prompt file, a json file, or a yaml file. Syntax looks like this:


### Examples


text:
```shell
stoked schedule [job-name] 0 0 * * * ./do_this_at_midnight.txt ./and_then_do_this.txt ./and_then_this.txt
```
json:
```shell
stoked schedule [job-name] 0 0 * * * ./midnight_job.json
```

```json
{
  "tasks": [
    {
      "name": "build tech updates email",
      "prompt": "create a reading list for any new technology news that seems relevant to me and send me an email with the list"
    },
    {
      "name": "schedule prep",
      "prompt": "read my scheudle for the next 3 days and give me a list of things that i should prepare for today in order to have successful tasks"
    }
  ]
}
```

yaml:
```shell
stoked schedule [job-name] 0 0 * * * ./midnight_job.yml
```

```yaml
---
tasks:
- name: build tech updates email
  prompt: create a reading list for any new technology news that seems relevant to
    me and send me an email with the list
- name: schedule prep
  prompt: read my scheudle for the next 3 days and give me a list of things that i
    should prepare for today in order to have successful tasks
```

issue.title: schedule command
issue.body:
### Search keywords

schedule command 

### Latest version

- [x] I have tested the latest version

### Summary

Create a schedule command that provides a unix cron syntax and a prompt to feed an llm on a given schedule. The following syntax should be the first supported:

stoked schedule 0 0 * * * ./run_everday_at_midnight.txt

This should schedule the task using a different library depending on the running operating system. Initially it should support linux, mac, and windows using node-linux, node-mac, and node-windows respectively so the host application does not need to be running in order to trigger the jobs since in this case the host will be an ephemeral cli that will definitely not be running.

### Examples

Create a top level schedule command that will provide instructions via prompt to an llm on a specific schedule using unix-cron format. An example of calling this command would look like the following:

stoked schedule 0 0 * * * ./do_this_task_at_midnight.txt

the command should consume the prompt provided and store it within the config at ~/.stoked/prompts.. 

### Motivation

_No response_
